citation_details.title: Benchmarking brain–computer interface algorithms: Riemannian approaches vs convolutional neural networks
citation_details.author: Manuel Eder, Jiachen Xu, Moritz Grosse‐Wentrup
citation_details.abstract: Abstract Objective. To date, a comprehensive comparison of Riemannian decoding methods with deep convolutional neural networks for EEG-based brain–computer interfaces remains absent from published work. We address this research gap by using MOABB, The Mother Of All BCI Benchmarks, to compare novel convolutional neural networks to state-of-the-art Riemannian approaches across a broad range of EEG datasets, including motor imagery, P300, and steady-state visual evoked potentials paradigms. Approach. We systematically evaluated the performance of convolutional neural networks, specifically EEGNet, shallow ConvNet, and deep ConvNet, against well-established Riemannian decoding methods using MOABB processing pipelines. This evaluation included within-session, cross-session, and cross-subject methods, to provide a practical analysis of model effectiveness and to find an overall solution that performs well across different experimental settings. citation_details.title: NeuroIDBench: An open-source benchmark framework for the standardization of methodology in brainwave-based authentication research
citation_details.author: Avinash Kumar Chaurasia, Matin Fallahi, Thorsten Strufe, Philipp Terhörst, Patricia Arias-Cabarcos
citation_details.venue: Journal of Information Security and Applications
citation_details.abstract: Biometric systems based on brain activity have been proposed as an alternative to passwords or to complement current authentication techniques. By leveraging the unique brainwave patterns of individuals, these systems offer the possibility of creating authentication solutions that are resistant to theft, hands-free, accessible, and potentially even revocable. However, despite the growing stream of research in this area, faster advance is hindered by reproducibility problems. Issues such as the lack of standard reporting schemes for performance results and system configuration, or the absence of common evaluation benchmarks, make comparability and proper assessment of different biometric solutions challenging. Further, barriers are erected to future work when, as so often, source code is not published open access. citation_details.abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of brain-computer interface, great breakthroughs have been made in the decoding of EEG signals. In particular, the feasibility of EEG signals as biometrics for identity has also been confirmed by many researchers. As a decoding technology, deep learning is widely used in the extraction of individual differences in EEG signals. However, the problem is that when designing deep learning networks, each researcher specifically responds to the EEG signal design network structure under a certain task paradigm, which is difficult to apply to other task data sets. Furthermore, data preprocessing and network structure are often complicated. Therefore, this paper proposes a convolutional neural network EEG identification scheme based on EEG topomap. citation_details.title: The Progress and Prospects of Data Capital for Zero-Shot Deep Brain–Computer Interfaces
citation_details.author: Wenbao Ma, Teng Ma, Daniel Organisciak, Jude E. T. Waide, Xiangxin Meng, Yang Long
citation_details.abstract: The vigorous development of deep learning (DL) has been propelled by big data and high-performance computing. For brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) to benefit from DL in a reliable and scalable manner, the scale and quality of data are crucial. Special emphasis is placed on the zero-shot learning (ZSL) paradigm, which is essential for enhancing the flexibility and scalability of BCI systems. ZSL enables models to generalise from limited examples to new, unseen tasks, addressing data scarcity challenges and accelerating the development of robust, adaptable BCIs. Despite a growing number of BCI surveys in recent years, there is a notable gap in clearly presenting public data resources. This paper explores the fundamental data capital necessary for large-scale deep learning BCI (DBCI) models. citation_details.title: P300 dataset BI2014a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
citation_details.author: Louis Korczowski, Ekaterina Ostaschenko, Anton Andreev, Grégoire Cattan, Pedro Luiz Coelho Rodrigues, Violette Gautheret, Marco Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 71 healthy subjects performing a visual P300-based brain-computer interface task using the Brain Invaders videogame. Participants engaged with an oddball paradigm involving pseudo-random flashes of 36 symbols on a grid to elicit P300 event-related potentials. The study evaluated the feasibility of a calibration-less P300 BCI system using 16 dry electrodes, with real-time adaptive classification for online feedback during gameplay. Subjects completed up to three game sessions.
